thread:
sara: Quick bring-up summary for OrionX-13B + quant sweep. Need a short GTN recommendation (cost vs quality) before EOD.

mike: Can you paste the quick numbers? product wants a one-liner they can act on.

sara: Paste from the slice-runner (sanity slices only):

```
Model             | Quant  | p50 lat(ms) | tok/s | rel_cost | qual_delta (eval score)
OrionX-13B fp16   | fp16   | 150         | 200   | 1.00     | +0.0
OrionX-13B int8   | int8   | 120         | 250   | 0.60     | -0.8
OrionX-13B int4   | int4   | 110         | 270   | 0.45     | -2.4
Midland-13B int8   | int8   | 130         | 230   | 0.65     | -0.3

Notes: rel_cost normalized to fp16 token cost. quality delta vs fp16 on product slices (higher is better).
```

anita: Thanks — where do the quality drops matter most? any catastrophic regressions on safety/longform?

sara: Short answer: majority of the drop for int8 is in multi-step factuality and some instruction-following for rare system prompts. Safety checks (toxicity) unchanged. For longform summarization we saw small hallucination uptick at int8 (-1.1 on longform slice).

kevin: What would you recommend for GTN routing? pure int8, hybrid, or hold in fp16?

sara: Proposed recommendation (for GTN/product):
- Default route: OrionX-13B int8 (primary) for 85% traffic — good cost wins (~40% tokens saved vs fp16) with small overall quality hit.
- Canaries & critical flows: route to fp16 (15%) for queries tagged as "longform" or "legal/finance" or explicit high-precision flags.
- Fallback: on quality/regression alerts (eval drift > 1.5 absolute on key slices) switch 100% to fp16 until triage.

anita: Any per-token economics + estimated monthly savings we can give to GTN? they like a $/M-token number.

sara: Rough math: baseline fp16 cost = $X per million tokens (use your standard $0.50/M as example). Using that: int8 effective cost = 0.6 * baseline -> $0.30/M. If GTN runs ~500M tokens/mo on this model, switching 85% to int8 => monthly savings ≈ (500M * 0.85) * ($0.50 - $0.30)/1M ≈ $85k/mo. (Tell them estimate, not SLA.)

mike: Good. We should add rollout guardrails and the eval checks to the ticket. Can you list the exact slices to monitor?

sara: Monitor these slices (initial):
- multi-step factuality
- longform summarization
- instruction-following (edge prompts)
- hallucination-sensitive product flows (billing/terms)
Also track latency p95 and token throughput so we don't regress infra economics.

kevin: For product: recommend flag name and initial %?

sara: Flag: gtn.orionx13b_quant_mode -> values: "fp16" or "int8". Start rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 85% over 7 days with automated quality checks at each step. If any key-slice drop > 1.0 absolute or p95 latency > 20% increase, pause and rollback.

anita: Sounds actionable. Can we include a short exec note for GTN: 1-2 sentences they can paste?

sara: Exec note (suggested):
"Recommend rolling OrionX-13B int8 as default for GTN (expected ~40% cost reduction vs fp16) with targeted fp16 routing for high-precision flows. Monitor key slices (multi-step factuality, longform) and use automated guardrails — rollback if core-slice eval drops >1.5 points."

mike: +1 from infra side. We'll add rollout playbook and a canary job in Jenkins.

ops-bot: canary-job/orionx13b-int8 started (job id 5521) :rocket:

sara: I'll open a tiny GH PR with the routing config and the slice checks, plus the summary above for GTN. tagging @mike @anita for review. :thumbsup:
